title: Implement the herdr backend behind the worker-backend trait
action: THIRD PASS on ho-8, and a narrow one. The second rework achieved its main goal: an independent judge re-ran all seven mutations against the Windows-compilable set and ALL SEVEN NOW DIE. Do not touch that work. The judge then went looking on its own and found three things the seven did not cover, plus a doc defect. Fix exactly these four. ITEM ONE, the one real behaviour still hidden behind the unix gate: canonical_id — D15's name-to-pane-id resolution — is the only interpretation step left inline in the trait method, with no pure function and no lib test. The judge collapsed it so a friendly name never resolves onto its pane id, which is the exact D15 defect an earlier judge found by execution, and the mutation SURVIVED the Windows set, dying only inside the gated file. Extract its interpretation into a pure function beside the others — given the agent-list bytes and a name, return the canonical id — and test it in the lib so the mutation dies on the Windows set. ITEM TWO: the Refuse arm of the start decision maps to an error at the trait boundary, and mutating that arm to succeed survives the Windows set, so start's refusal is unproven there end to end. Pin it with a pure test. ITEM THREE, the sharpest of the three: replacing the constructed agent_args with an empty slice at the call site SURVIVES ALL 71 FLEET TESTS. Nothing at any tier proves the constructed agent arguments actually reach the argv — the pure function is tested and the field is set, but the leg joining them is proven only by reading. Add the test that kills that mutation, and prefer a pure one so it runs on Windows. ITEM FOUR: the constructor's own doc never names herding.agent_command, never says token 0 becomes the kind, and never mentions D14's typed error. It defers to the agent_kind field's doc, but that field is PRIVATE, so rustdoc does not render it on the struct page — the judge built the docs and grepped the rendered HTML to confirm the pointer is silently dead. cargo doc emitted no warning because the reference is backticked prose rather than an intra-doc link. Put the obligation on the constructor doc itself, in words, where a caller meets it. VERIFY THE WAY THE JUDGE DID: re-run all three mutations from items one to three against cargo test -p fleet --lib --test choreography --test manifest_boundary and report each as dying. A mutation that still survives is the cell unfinished.

truths: canonical_id's interpretation is a pure function tested in the lib, and collapsing it so a name never resolves to its pane id dies on the Windows-compilable set.
The start refusal arm is pinned by a pure test, and mutating it to succeed dies on the Windows-compilable set.
Replacing the constructed agent_args with an empty slice at the call site now fails a test, and that test runs on the Windows-compilable set.
All three mutations were re-run and reported as dying — observed, not assumed.
The constructor's own documentation names herding.agent_command, says token 0 becomes the kind, and states that raising D14's typed error for an unrecognised value is the caller's obligation.
The seven mutations from the previous pass still die.
No assertion anywhere was deleted or loosened.
prohibitions: Do not undo the pure-versus-process split — it is what made the seven mutations die.
Do not read bee configuration from the fleet crate.
Do not delete or weaken any existing test; the gated duplicates may stay.
Do not add a dependency or an async runtime.
Do not implement the bee-side wave verb — that is D17's own cell.

trace.outcome: Implemented HerdrBackend (WorkerBackend over the real herdr CLI) beside the fake, closed D15's canonical-identity gap with a new canonical_id trait method the choreography dedupes on, and added the three hazard tests plus fail-closed status coverage via a PATH-prepended stub herdr

report.outcome: Implemented HerdrBackend beside the fake, closed D15's canonical-identity gap, added the three hazard tests plus fail-closed status coverage
report.tests: PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test --release --manifest-path packages/bee-rs/Cargo.toml — green — full declared verify command run, whole workspace including fleet's 57 tests (23 unit + 11 choreography + 17 herdr_backend + 6 manifest_boundary) and bee's 1887 tests unaffected
deviations: HerdrBackend's WorkerSpec::name contract for herdr is a herdr pane id (already split by the caller) or a friendly agent name already known to herdr; start() refuses rather than fabricate a pane-splitting spawn since WorkerSpec carries no cwd — that wiring is D17's deferred bee-side wave verb, not this cell
agent list's per-agent JSON shape is inferred beyond spawn-proof.md, which does not show it byte-for-byte; parsing fails closed to Unverifiable/Err on any mismatch rather than guessing further
the herdr_backend.rs stub-binary test suite is cfg(unix) only — no Windows-native stub equivalent yet, a named gap; the pure status-mapping unit tests inside herdr.rs itself are cross-platform

checks.evidence: No fail-open path found. map_status has no safe-default arm; status folds spawn failure, non-zero exit, unparseable body, target-absent and missing-or-null agent_status all into Unverifiable. Mutation-tested on a scratchpad copy with cargo test -p fleet after each single-line mutation: off-enum arm to Ready, lookup-error arm to Ready, target-absent to Ready, missing field to Ready, and the unknown mapping to Finished — 5 of 5 caught by named tests. Two cases correct by construction but untested: an explicit JSON null agent_status (only the missing-key case has a test; both take the same and_then arm) and a null pane_id in canonical_id. Caveat carried into H5: three of the five catching tests live in the cfg(unix)-gated suite.

WorkerBackend::canonical_id exists and resolve_and_dedupe keys on its result rather than the raw name. The choreography holds no herdr knowledge: a case-insensitive search for herdr, pane, worktree, cell, lane, gate and proof across choreography.rs, wave.rs and lib.rs returned exactly one hit, a doc-comment example. Mutation-tested: deduping on the raw name is caught by invariant_8_a_name_and_its_backend_side_pane_id_collapse_to_one_target, and so is a variant where the choreography short-circuits on a colon in the identifier — that is, where it learns herdr's pane-id shape. The invariant 8 test asserts quantitatively through fake-backend counters rather than by eye.

All three hazard tests exist in tests/herdr_backend.rs and each pins what it names. The already-working-agent test asserts the recorded argv carries no --wait, and adding --wait to the prompt argv is caught. The oversized-reply test uses a 50,000-character spill file, and disabling the spill-recovery branch is caught. The unfocused-status test drives a done status with focused false and asserts agent list is the only herdr call; making status return Unverifiable unless focused is true is caught by it and by one other. 3 of 3 caught. Caveat: all three live in the cfg(unix)-gated file — see H5.

The diff of tests/choreography.rs between c945e4ae and 76656a11 is 87 insertions and zero deletions. The only edits to pre-existing tests are added doc comments; every assertion is byte-identical. The new invariant 8 test is additive. The fake backend gains alias, canonical_id and two call counters; its one behavioural change is read_output switching to an entry-or-default so it can count calls, which returns the same value for a known worker and an empty string for an unknown one, identical to the prior behaviour.

tests/herdr_backend.rs is gated by a file-level cfg(unix). Test counts: lib 23, choreography 11, herdr_backend 17, manifest_boundary 6 — so 17 of 57 fleet tests, 30 percent, do not run on Windows, and they are every test that drives the backend against a process. What survives on Windows is four pure-function unit tests. Concretely: the five-string status map has Windows coverage, but the fail-closed folding of lookup failures has NONE; the generic half of canonical identity is covered, the herdr resolution half is NOT; and the three hazards have zero Windows coverage. Measured rather than argued — re-running each mutation with only the test set Windows would compile gives SURVIVED for all seven: lookup-error fails open, target-absent fails open, missing or null field fails open, send passes --wait, spill recovery deleted, status requires focus, and start silently returning Ok instead of refusing. On Windows the backend could do all of that and CI would stay green. This contradicts D4, which makes Windows a required outcome rather than a follow-up, and contradicts the Windows workflow's own stated policy that the Rust suite has no split, runs unexcluded, and that a Windows-only failure is a real failure rather than a suite to add to a skip list. This cell added exactly such a skip list. The file header names the gap, but its mitigation claim covers only four of the seventeen and none of the three hazards.

The deferral boundary is only half real, and the half that is not real is pinned green. WorkerSpec does carry only name and task, so that premise is honest. But HerdrBackend::start does not simply refuse: it refuses only a never-seen, non-pane-id-shaped name. For a pane-id-shaped name it spawns for real and invents the agent kind, passing --kind claude as a hardcoded literal, and a test now PINS that hardcode by asserting the invocation starts with agent start w4-pB --kind claude --pane w4:pB. D14 requires --kind to be derived from herding.agent_command token 0, with an unrecognised token 0 surfacing as a typed error naming the key. The one path the cell claims it deferred to D17 is the exact path it silently implemented with a wrong constant, and a green test now defends it — the silent-drift class D13 and D14 exist to prevent. What D17's cell now owes: replace the hardcoded kind with the config-derived one plus D14's typed error, and un-pin the test asserting the constant; supply a cwd and kind carrying spec so start no longer guesses a slug from the pane id; and restore the caller's tab focus after agent start, which the code explicitly declines to do. ORCHESTRATOR CORRECTION, recorded because a verdict must not carry a claim known to be false: the judge also reported that D15, D16 and D17 have no decision record behind their cited hashes, having searched the worktree's own git-tracked copy of the decision log. That copy is frozen at the branch point by construction. The control root's store holds all three hashes; the decisions exist. The real and related gap, which was genuine, is that CONTEXT.md's locked table stopped at D14 — fixed in commit 6e2db85b.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: The herdr backend's behaviour is entirely unproven on Windows: 17 of 57 fleet tests sit behind a file-level cfg(unix), and 7 of 7 backend mutations SURVIVE a run restricted to the tests Windows compiles, against D4's required-outcome and the Windows workflow's explicit no-skip-list policy. Separately, HerdrBackend::start hardcodes --kind claude and a new test pins that constant green, contradicting D14 and the very D17 boundary the cell claims to defer.

checks.evidence: Run on a scratchpad copy, one mutation at a time, the file restored from a pristine copy between runs, using exactly cargo test -p fleet --lib --test choreography --test manifest_boundary. Baseline green at 37 lib plus 11 choreography plus 6 manifest_boundary, 54 total. All seven die: the lookup-error arm returning Ready dies on interpret_status_lookup_is_unverifiable_on_a_failed_lookup; the target-absent arm dies on interpret_status_lookup_is_unverifiable_when_the_target_is_absent; the missing-or-null agent_status arm dies on interpret_status_lookup_is_unverifiable_when_agent_status_is_missing_or_null; inserting --wait into the prompt argv dies on build_prompt_argv_never_includes_wait; disabling spill recovery dies on recover_transcript_reads_the_spill_file_when_the_last_line_hands_back_its_path; gating status on focused being true dies on interpret_status_lookup_does_not_depend_on_the_pane_having_been_focused; and start silently returning Ok dies on decide_start_refuses_a_never_seen_non_pane_shaped_name_rather_than_fabricate_a_spawn. Seven of seven die on the Windows-compilable set; none survives.

Seventeen tests remain behind the file-level cfg(unix) gate. Thirteen of them duplicate the pure tests, which V1 proves. The other four do not: canonical_id's D15 name-to-pane-id resolution is the one interpretation step the rework left inline in the trait method, with no pure function and no lib test. Collapsing it so a friendly name never resolves onto its pane id — the exact D15 defect an earlier judge found by execution — SURVIVES the Windows set at 37, 11 and 6 all ok, and dies only inside the gated file. Two further glue arms are likewise Windows-invisible: the Refuse arm mapping to Ok means start's refusal is unproven on Windows end to end and survives the Windows set; and replacing the constructed agent_args with an empty slice at the call site SURVIVES THE ENTIRE FLEET SUITE of 71 tests, so no test at any tier proves the constructed agent arguments reach the argv. The gate therefore still hides one real behaviour plus two unproven wiring arms.

No kind literal remains in production code: the only argv site pushes the --kind flag followed by the constructed value, and every other occurrence of the string is doc prose or a test argument. Mutating both constructors to discard the parameter and substitute the old literal is not caught by the Windows set but IS caught by the full suite, on start_spawns_a_fresh_agent_using_the_constructed_kind_never_a_hardcoded_literal, whose failure quotes the argv it got. The kind is genuinely constructed rather than defaulted. The agent arguments are appended after a literal double dash, asserted by decide_start_appends_agent_args_after_a_literal_double_dash and by the omission case, both pure and both green on the Windows set. Caveat carried into V2: only the pure leg is proven — the constructor-to-argv leg survives its mutation across all 71 tests.

The constructor's own documentation says the backend resolves herdr off the host PATH, that long replies spill to the OS temp directory, and that every spawned agent is started with the agent kind and arguments already resolved by the caller, deferring to the agent_kind field's own docs. It never names herding.agent_command, never says token 0 becomes the kind, and never mentions the typed error for an unrecognised value. The field it defers to is PRIVATE, so rustdoc does not render it on the struct page — verified by building the docs and grepping the rendered HTML, where the struct page carries no match and only the module page does. cargo doc emitted no warning because the reference is backticked prose rather than an intra-doc link, so the pointer is silently dead in rendered form. The obligation exists in the module docs; it is absent from the constructor doc where the caller meets it.

The rework commit touches exactly two files. The test diff is sixteen insertions and five deletions across three hunks: a new constructor helper, one test renamed from the pane-id spawn case to the constructed-kind case with the helper swapped in, and the assertion tightened from the old literal to a different constructed kind, keeping the same predicate with a stronger message. The test inventory is seventeen names before and seventeen after, one renamed, none deleted. The four pre-existing pure tests survive byte-identical and eleven were added, taking the lib count from twenty-six to thirty-seven. In substance the status map is unchanged, the fail-closed fold is character-for-character the body now living in the pure interpretation function, canonical_id is byte-identical to its previous form, and the spill recovery is the previous body relocated. No assertion was deleted or loosened.

The manifest diff across the rework is empty, so no dependency was added. The fleet manifest lists only anyhow, serde and serde_json, carries no bee path dependency, and the manifest boundary test passes in every run. A search for an async runtime, await points, or any read of bee state finds none; the only environment access builds the child process PATH rather than reading bee configuration. The module's imports are std process and path types, serde_json, and the crate's own trait and wave types — nothing from bee.

semantic_judge.failure_signature: The unix gate still hides one real behaviour and two unproven wiring arms: canonical_id's D15 name-to-pane-id resolution has no pure function and no lib test, so collapsing it survives the Windows-compilable set and dies only in the gated file; the Refuse-to-error arm likewise survives that set; and replacing the constructed agent_args with an empty slice survives all 71 fleet tests, so nothing proves the constructed arguments reach the argv. Separately, the constructor's doc omits the D14 obligation entirely, deferring to a private field doc that rustdoc never renders on the struct page.
